subject: Private deployment: sustained p99 spikes, decode errors and throughput churn - remediation plan
messages:
From: Rebecca Tran <rebecca.tran@stanleyhealth.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@stanleyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: (urgent) Private cluster degradation - requests and logs attached

Alex —

We woke up to a pretty bad deterioration across our private VPC deployment. Since ~05:00 PST we've seen sustained p99 increases (from ~420ms to ~2.8s), a growing number of decode errors (502/5xx on model decode stage), and overall throughput drop by ~38%. This is impacting live inference for triage routing and the on-call queues are filling.

Attached are the logs (stanley_logs_20261124.txt) and a KV cache snapshot we pulled earlier. We are running Redwood Private (v1.9.3) in our GCP VPC, 6 40GB A100s, pinned to the rlnet-quant profile. We did not change traffic config overnight.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood treat this as an incident and provide a mitigation plan within 3 hours?
- We need an ETA for full remediation or a durable fallback (hosted fallback or scaling instructions).
- Please advise if you need any more captures (traces, sysmetrics).

Thanks — this is materially impacting our support SLA.

—Rebecca
Head of Platform — Stanley Health

Attachment: stanley_logs_20261124.txt (text/plain, 1.2MB)
Attachment: kv_cache_snapshot_20261124.json (application/json, 200KB)
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: (urgent) Private cluster degradation - triage + short-term mitigations

Team — Rebecca sent the logs above. Stanley's private cluster (6x A100) is seeing sustained p99 spikes, decode 5xxs, and throughput collapse. This is a Priority P1 for the customer; they asked for a plan within 3 hours.

Initial thoughts: can we confirm whether this looks like KV cache thrashing, NVLINK degradation, or a model-side regression (kernel path)? Naomi, can you do a quick diagnostic pass and recommend 1-2 immediate mitigations we can propose publicly?

Options to consider for customer-facing mitigations:
- Temporary routing to our hosted inference pool for the most latency-sensitive endpoints (if acceptable to customer).
- Increase KV cache allocation / pin hot prefixes to avoid evictions.
- Rollback to the last-known-good model artifact or switch to a lower-latency quantized variant.
- Short-term add capacity (burst) to the private pool if policy allows.

Marissa — please prepare a customer-facing response with a clear mitigation timeline and options (including tradeoffs and any credits we should offer). Rishi — flag for commercial (credits / escalation).

I'll be on the bridge for triage.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai

To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Fwd: (urgent) Private cluster degradation - triage + short-term mitigations

Quick diagnostic summary (first-pass):
- Observed signal: repeated KV cache evictions correlated with p99 spikes. The KV hit rate dropped from 92% to ~61% starting ~04:50 PST.
- Decode layer: a subset of requests hit a new execution path that triggers a slower kernel (likely due to a rare autocast/format detection). 5xxs are concentrated on nodes 3 and 4.
- Host-level: node 4 shows elevated GPU-to-GPU latency and some transient NVLINK retransmits; disk i/o on node 3 shows higher write stall time (likely checkpointing collision).

Proposed immediate mitigations (can be executed in the next 60-90 minutes):
1) Increase KV cache reserved allocation for the model (config: kv_cache_reserve: +25%). This should reduce eviction churn; low risk.
2) Move a small % (5-10%) of traffic for most latency-sensitive endpoints to our hosted pool (fallback). This requires customer sign-off (data routing implications).
3) Evict and reprovision node 4 (hot node) after draining traffic for 10 minutes — we can do a rolling reprovision to avoid a full outage.
4) Apply a hotfix to the runtime that forces the older kernel path for the failing execution branch (rollback kernel selector) — medium risk, validated on staging.

Data we still need: full perf trace (nvprof) for the slow requests and the model artifact id (sha) currently pinned. Rebecca — can you send the model artifact/version and confirm whether you are comfortable routing a small percentage to hosted while we remediate?

I'll open JIRA INF-9472 and attach the traces. If we get sign-off, we can begin steps 1 and 3 immediately; step 4 will need a 30-minute validation window on staging.

-Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Attachment referenced: kv_cache_snapshot_20261124.json (used for hit-rate analysis)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Tran <rebecca.tran@stanleyhealth.com>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: (urgent) Private cluster degradation - customer mitigation plan

Rebecca — thank you for the logs and patience. Per Naomi's triage, we have a short plan and clear next steps. I'm sending this to you with explicit items and timings so you can share with your ops execs.

Customer-facing mitigation proposal (opt-in):
- T+0 to T+30 minutes: Increase kv_cache_reserve by 25% (non-disruptive). Redwood will execute and monitor.
- T+30 to T+60 minutes: Drain node 4 and reprovision (rolling). This will impact capacity but we will maintain availability by redistributing traffic.
- T+60 to T+120 minutes: If p99 remains elevated, we will route 5-10% of traffic to Redwood hosted fallback while Naomi validates the kernel rollback on staging (we will only route after written sign-off).
- T+120 to T+240 minutes: Apply kernel selector hotfix if validated. Full validation on staging required.

Business considerations:
- If you approve hosted fallback routing, we will redact PII/PHI per the routing agreement and we can sign an addendum if needed.
- Redwood commercial will review a one-time credit for the impacted window. Rishi — please propose a dollar estimate for credits ASAP.

Request: Please confirm (1) approval to increase KV cache reserve now and (2) whether we have permission to route 5% traffic to hosted fallback if the first fixes do not restore latency.

I can be on the customer bridge at 2pm PST for a live huddle. If you'd prefer an executive bridge, we can include our Head of Customer Success.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Business note: this impacts our critical incident escalation metrics; we will expect a commercial credit for the incident window — happy to take a proposal from Rishi and finance. We also need an executive-level summary after remediation outlining root cause, timeline, and long-term mitigation.

2pm PST bridge works for us. Please send calendar invite and bridge details.

—Rebecca
